readout_other: DeepLabCut-based tracking of freely-moving locomotion (speed, cumulative distance) to assess the mechanical/weight burden of the head-mounted device; no ultrasound was actually delivered during this in vivo behavioural test (the CMUT was untethered/unpowered), so no biological effect of sonication was measured in vivo.
safety_notes: Only the mechanical burden of wearing the device was assessed (no significant change in locomotion speed or distance travelled between Normal, Sham-surgery and Device groups); no biological/tissue safety assessment of active sonication was performed in this study.

exposures.label: CMUT + skull-compensated acoustic lens, bench/ex vivo skull acoustic characterization (2 MHz)

target.label: no specific in vivo brain target stimulated; system designed for versatile/multi-region targeting, characterized on a skull phantom and an ex vivo mouse skull

timing.protocol_description: This paper reports device design/fabrication (a CMUT planar transducer combined with a 3D-printed, time-reversal-mirror acoustic lens for skull-aberration-compensated multifocal targeting) and its bench-top and ex vivo acoustic characterization; no live-animal ultrasound stimulation session (pulse timing, dose, or duration) is described. The only in vivo animal work was a freely-moving locomotion test of mice wearing the unpowered/untethered device to assess its physical burden.

source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: Using fast Fourier transform (FFT) analysis of the response signal for a 100-ns-wide rectangular pulse of 10 V amplitude with 42 V of DC bias, the center frequency and bandwidth were measured to be 2 MHz and 1.5 MHz, respectively (Fig. 4f).
source_quotes.exposures[0].in_situ.pressure_kpa: The peak pressure amplitude was 44.6 kPa with a DC bias of 42 V and peak-to-peak AC swing of 5 V, which was sufficient for neuromodulation<sup>55</sup>.
source_quotes.exposures[0].in_situ.method: A mouse skull was harvested ex vivo and packaged with the device according to the same coordinate-based alignment protocol as the in vivo experiment. Then, the acoustic pressure profile was directly measured by scanning the needle hydrophone within the half-skull cavity (Fig. S12).
source_quotes.sham_type: To evaluate the effects of the attached package on mouse behavioral studies, the freely moving behaviors of mice with the package affixed to the head were analyzed.

flags.reason: This is primarily a device-engineering paper; no in vivo ultrasound neuromodulation session with a defined brain target/dose was performed. The single exposure entry reports bench-top/ex vivo-skull acoustic characterization values (2 MHz CMUT + lens) rather than an actual stimulation protocol; target, timing and most dose fields are not applicable/not reported.
The 87.7 kPa value is the bare CMUT output measured in oil (no lens, no skull), so it is not clearly a water/free-field or an in-brain value; placed in unspecified_domain.

Nine mice were used for the freely-moving behavioural (device-burden) test, but none received active ultrasound stimulation in vivo in this study, so n_subjects (exposed to ultrasound) is not_reported rather than 9.
No biological/tissue safety assessment of active sonication was reported; only device-wearing behavioural burden was assessed.

direction_notes: Direction of effect was not assessed in vivo: the only live-animal experiment measured locomotion while wearing the unpowered device, not a neural or behavioural response to active sonication.
